Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Attached: Q1 rate card + a short explainer. TL;DR up top, full detail below.

TL;DR:
- "Responses" (the newer unified endpoint) is billed per token: both input tokens (prompt/messages) + output tokens (generated tokens). System messages and function-call payloads are included in the input token count; when a function returns structured JSON the tokens in that JSON are counted as output tokens.
- "Chat Completions" (legacy) uses a similar token model but historically had different SKUs and per-token rates — we are keeping legacy rates active until migration, then apply Responses pricing.
- Streaming does not change pricing mechanics — you are billed for the same tokens whether you stream or receive full responses at once.

Quick notes on specifics you asked for:
- Function calls: when the model emits a function call we bill the tokens for the call name + arguments as output tokens (they are generated by the model). If your function then returns additional payloads via your application, those are not billed by us unless you send them back to the model as part of a new request.
- System messages and hidden/meta messages: counted as part of the input token bundle when submitted to the endpoint.
- Message framing: Responses serializes message arrays into tokens — there is no per-message surcharge, only token counts.
- Legacy endpoints: same token counting logic, but check the rate_card PDF for legacy SKU offsets (some customers have grandfathered rates for completions endpoints).
- Batching and caching: suggestions on batching window sizes and prefix caching can materially reduce billed tokens; happy to connect you with solutions engineering on optimization.

Commit discounts and overages:
- We offer volume tiers and committed monthly spend contracts (MOP). Example tiers: 0–250M tokens, 250M–1B, 1B+. Committed discounts can range from 10–25% depending on term and commitment.
- Overages above committed amounts are charged at a post-discount overage rate; we do a monthly true-up.
- We can structure quarterly or annual true-ups and include minimum monthly guarantees in the contract.

Attachments included:
- rate_card_Q1_2026.pdf (full SKU table + legacy comparison)
- short_explainer_responses_vs_completions.pdf (single-page summary)

If you can share an expected token mix (ratio of input to output, estimated % of function-calling traffic), I can run a modeled spend and propose a committed tier.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
